text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH SEV - possible cross-tenant prefix echo detected in dedicated pool 'pool-ded-33'. Trigger: anomalous routing prefix overlap observed between tenants 'helio-meds' and 'orion-labs'. Auto-rate: page oncall.

kyra: I’m on it. pulling logs for pool-ded-33 now. can someone grab customer-facing context? which tenants live there? @lee-support

lee-support: Helio-Meds and Orion-Labs both have reserved capacity in that pool, yes. Helio's traffic started spiking ~08:12 UTC. no customer ticket yet.

omar: what alerted? any request bodies leaking or just route metadata?

incident-bot: Alert details: routing-service matched prefix 10.24.188.0/24 to tenant helio-meds at 08:11:42, same source-ip later delivered to tenant orion-labs at 08:11:45. Confidence: medium. Sample traces attached to alert (trace ids: t-8a3, t-8a4).

jen-sre: reproducing quick checks. running log grep across router proxies.

jen-sre: ```
redwoodctl pool inspect pool-ded-33 --json | jq '.active_tenants'
redwoodctl logs tail --pool pool-ded-33 --since 30m | grep -E "helio-meds|orion-labs" | head -50
```

jen-sre: grep shows 172 hits where requests tagged tenant=helio-meds were forwarded to backend with tenant=orion-labs routing header. grabbing first sample.

kyra: ok that’s actionable. omar, can you check model-serving layer for any shared cache/prefixing? possible prefix key collision in routing cache.

omar: on it. checking redis/kvcache layers and the routing table join logic. running quick probe:

omar: ```
redwoodctl cache scan --pool pool-ded-33 --key-pattern "prefix:*" | grep "10.24.188"
# then
redwoodctl cache dump --key prefix:10.24.188.23
```

omar: found 1 entry where prefix:10.24.188.23 has metadata tenant=helio-meds but cached backend pointer -> orion-labs-backend-3. Looks like cache pointer stale after a backend reassignment.

security-ops: tagging as potential data-routing exposure. we need isolation now. recommended immediate mitigations: (1) disable prefix caching for pool-ded-33, (2) evict routing-cache pods, (3) perform safe snapshot + audit of traces.

kyra: I’ll run mitigations. executing step 1.

kyra: ```
redwoodctl config set service.routing.cache.enabled false --scope pool:pool-ded-33
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/routing-cache-pool-ded-33
```

deploy-bot: Received rollout restart request for deployment/routing-cache-pool-ded-33 by kyra. Restart initiated.

jen-sre: eviction in progress. rolling restart shows pods terminating gracefully. taking snapshot of cache and routing logs to S3://incidents/2074123456/evidence.tar.gz

lee-support: communicating to Helio-Meds and Orion-Labs engineering contacts. draft msg in INC-2074 (internal) — will follow customer comms once we have impact summary. keeping it blameless.

oncall-ml: quick question — is this only routing metadata or any user payload observed in cross-delivery?

jen-sre: initial samples show only routing headers and metadata leaked, no full request bodies. still verifying.

omar: root cause hypothesis: a race during backend reattach after resizing caused routing-cache to write a stale backend pointer without tenant-scoping in the pointer key. cache key included prefix but not tenant id in v1.3.1. newer version v1.3.2 includes tenant-scoped keys.

nate-pm: action items: 1) keep pool isolated until audit complete, 2) notify impacted customers, 3) remediate service to v1.3.2 in pool-ded-33, 4) run post-incident data-access audit. ETA for v1.3.2 rollout?

omar: can push v1.3.2 to pool in ~18m once we confirm smoke tests. migration will use tenant-scoped keys and flush stale pointers.

kyra: initiating node-level isolation for Helio-Meds as precaution: applying prefix block and creating temporary route override to pin Helio traffic to dedicated fallback nodes.

kyra: ```
redwoodctl route override add --pool pool-ded-33 --tenant helio-meds --node-group fallback-helio
redwoodctl firewall add --scope pool:pool-ded-33 --src-prefix 10.24.188.0/24 --action drop --reason "isolation - incident 2074123456"
```

jen-sre: cache rollbacks complete, v1.3.2 deploy queued in canary. monitoring for errors.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for routing-cache v1.3.2 in pool-ded-33 (5% nodes).

security-ops: collecting timeline & evidence for compliance. set incident severity to Sev2 (no confirmed PII exfil yet). creating incident record INC-2074123456 in pagerduty and jira INC-2074.

lee-support: customer comms draft posted to INC-2074: "We detected anomalous routing metadata overlap, we've isolated traffic and are rolling a fix. No evidence of request body exposure. We'll follow up within 2 hours with a summary." sending now to Helio-Meds as a cautious notice.

oncall-ml: smoke tests on canary look good. no cross-delivery observed after cache disable + v1.3.2 canary.

omar: starting flush of stale pointers and final cache migration.

omar: ```
redwoodctl cache delete --pool pool-ded-33 --key-pattern "prefix:*"
# then verify
redwoodctl cache verify --pool pool-ded-33 --mode tenant-scoped
```

jen-sre: flush complete. triggered end-to-end test between tenants. PASS.

kyra: lifting temporary firewall for Helio after validation, keeping route override for 15m to observe.

kyra: ```
redwoodctl firewall delete --scope pool:pool-ded-33 --rule "isolation - incident 2074123456"
```

security-ops: final verdict pending audit, but all mitigations applied and canary->full rollout working. recommended next steps: full audit of logs for 24h, customer post-incident report, root cause doc + retro.

nate-pm: assigning follow-ups: INC-2074-1 (audit), INC-2074-2 (post-incident customer report), INC-2074-3 (ensure tenant id enforced in cache keys across all pools). due EOD.

lee-support: will follow up to customers with a summary and offer dedicated support call. closing interim comms: "we've mitigated risk, will share findings in incident report." 

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied at 08:32 UTC (cache disable + eviction), fix deployed at 08:48 UTC (routing-cache v1.3.2), traffic pinned and validated; monitoring normal. Incident remains open until audit complete. (INC-2074123456)
